atoms.text: Rosa Parks was born on the 4th of February, 1913 and lived in Montgomery, Alabama in the United States. On the 1st of December, 1955 she took the bus home after work. At the time, the first rows of seats were reserved for 'whites only'. Black people were forced to sit in the back of the bus.
On this day, the bus driver demanded that Rosa, who was black, move, so a white person could sit. Rosa refused. Her refusal led to her arrest and a fine. However, it also started a movement.

After her arrest, many black ministers spread the news about what Rosa did in church. They called for a boycott until the city changed its laws. More than 40,000 people stopped taking the bus in Montgomery.

hint.text: A boycott is the act of not doing something, buying something, or going somewhere, until what you wanted to happen has been forced to happen.
hint.label: Boycott

atoms.text: As a result, in December 1956, the unfair seating order in buses finally ended. From then on, black people could sit wherever they wished on the bus. Rosa Parks died in October 2005. However, to this day, many people in the US do not take the bus on the 1st of December and the 4th of February to honour her actions.
In 2013, Rosa became the first black woman to be honoured with a statue in the United States Capitol.
